stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates continued community interest and usage of Meta's Llama models within the AI ecosystem.

stories.title: Microsoft confirms Copilot ‘super app’ coming this year
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Microsoft is developing an AI 'super app' centered around Copilot.
This new application will integrate Copilot's chat, coding, and agentic functionalities.
The super app is slated for release this year and will serve both consumer and commercial markets.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg is planning a big push into personal AI agents
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta is heavily investing in AI and planning a major expansion into personal AI agents.
CEO Mark Zuckerberg outlined a high-level vision for these personal agents during the Q2 2026 earnings call.
The move signals Meta's commitment to integrating AI deeply into user workflows to perform tasks on their behalf.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its capability in conversational AI.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a generative AI model.
The tags confirm its association with major AI frameworks (transformers, safetensors) and the Llama family.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured $88 million in funding from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
The company boasts a significant developer base, serving 8.9 million developers.
The news highlights the growing adoption and investment in open-source large language models (LLMs) via Ollama.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The optimized engine results in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets and optimizes performance on Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring data processing occurs entirely on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: Xbox revenue drops 10 percent as Microsoft’s cloud and AI business surges
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Xbox revenue experienced a 10% drop, driven by declines in content and services like Game Pass.
Xbox hardware sales saw a 13% decline in the latest quarterly report.
This downturn is contrasted by a surge in Microsoft's overall cloud and AI business segments.

stories.title: OpenAI president says it’s ‘building a family of devices’ for its AI chatbots
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: OpenAI is developing a 'family of devices' designed for interaction with its AI chatbots.
The announcement comes from OpenAI president Greg Brockman in an interview.
The company did not confirm rumors regarding a specific smart speaker launch date (e.g., 2027).

stories.title: Mythos attack on 3rd-round PQC algorithm candidate puts it out of commission
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability was discovered in the HAWK algorithm candidate using the Mythos attack.
The discovery invalidates years of prior testing and validation for the PQC candidate.
This represents a significant setback in the development and standardization of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).

stories.title: Anthropic is finding bugs faster than Microsoft can fix them
stories.author: Renee Dudley, ProPublica
bullet_points: Anthropic is reportedly discovering security vulnerabilities in its models at a faster rate than Microsoft can patch them.
The situation indicates a significant and ongoing security race between AI developers and potential attackers.
Microsoft is reportedly engaged in an urgent, behind-the-scenes effort to address these exploits.

stories.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
stories.author: Arvind Narayanan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical, yet unproven, hypothesis that AI agents can autonomously conduct open-ended AI research.
It critiques existing evaluation methods, which are either too narrow or rely on unreliable peer review processes.
The authors propose a novel methodology to measure progress toward automating AI Research and Development (R&D).

stories.title: APEX-Accounting
stories.author: Bertie Vidgen
bullet_points: Introduction of APEX-Accounting, a new benchmark designed to test frontier AI models on real-world accounting tasks.
The benchmark assesses complex accounting functions such as account reconciliation, expense accrual, and report generation.
The evaluation uses a private set of 160 tasks across 10 simulated worlds, authored and solved by accounting experts.

stories.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
stories.author: Arvind Narayanan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical, yet unproven, concept of AI agents conducting open-ended AI research.
It critiques existing evaluation methods, noting that current tests are either too narrow or rely on unreliable peer review.
The authors propose a novel methodology to measure progress toward automating AI Research & Development (R&D).

stories.title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: Introduces 'MindForge,' a new approach to teach small Language Models (LLMs) the entire software engineering lifecycle.
Addresses the critical challenge of 'from-scratch' program synthesis, where current frontier models struggle with over 99% of tasks.
Proposes a solution to the lack of scalable training environments necessary for comprehensive, end-to-end software engineering training.

stories.title: APEX-Accounting
stories.author: Bertie Vidgen
bullet_points: Introduction of APEX-Accounting, a new benchmark designed to test frontier models' capabilities in real-world accounting tasks.
The benchmark, developed by Mercor and Ramp, covers complex functions like account reconciliation, expense accrual, and report generation.
The private evaluation set consists of 160 expert-authored tasks across 10 distinct 'worlds,' incorporating various document types (spreadsheets, PDFs).

stories.title: DenseOn with the LateOn: Fully Open Dense and Late-Interaction Models for Multilingual, Long-Context, and Code Search
stories.author: Amélie Chatelain
bullet_points: Introduces DenseOn with LateOn, a fully open model architecture for dense and late-interaction retrieval.
Addresses the reproducibility gap in SOTA retrieval models by providing an open end-to-end training recipe.
Demonstrates cross-lingual transferability by using 'translate-train' to leverage English supervision for multilingual retrieval.

stories.title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: Introduces 'MindForge,' a method to teach small Language Models (LLMs) the entire software engineering lifecycle.
Addresses the significant challenge of 'from-scratch' program synthesis, where current frontier models perform poorly (under 1% on ProgramBench).
Overcomes the limitation of lacking scalable training environments that cover the full scope of software engineering tasks.

stories.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment
stories.author: Sheng Wen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical vulnerability in LLM fine-tuning where malicious data can embed harmful behaviors.
Proposes 'On-Policy Distillation' with a routing approach to achieve template-robust safety realignment.
Overcomes limitations of existing safety defenses, such as catastrophic forgetting of specialized skills.

stories.title: Show HN: Open-source engine running Gemma 4 26B in 2 GB RAM on any M-series Mac
stories.author: gitpusher42
bullet_points: A new open-source inference engine, TurboFieldfare, allows running large language models on consumer hardware.
The engine successfully runs the 4-bit quantized Gemma 4 26B model using only ~2 GB of RAM on M-series Macs.
The project highlights the growing trend and feasibility of powerful on-device AI applications.

stories.title: Slopsquatting: The Supply Chain Attack That Weaponizes AI Hallucinations
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: Introduces 'Slopsquatting,' a novel supply chain attack vector leveraging AI hallucinations.
Compares it to typosquatting, suggesting AI assistants are a new vulnerability surface.
Highlights the risk where AI models invent or generate malicious/incorrect code/components.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware platforms.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM integration.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local AI model execution via Ollama.

stories.title: Qualcomm is raising phone chip prices starting September 1st
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Qualcomm is implementing price increases across its range of phone processors.
The price hikes are scheduled to take effect starting September 1st.
The announcement was made by Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon, following prior rumors.

stories.title: xAI’s last-minute scramble to stop Minnesota’s anti-nudification app law
stories.author: Sarah Jeong
bullet_points: xAI is legally challenging a Minnesota law targeting 'nudification' apps.
The company argues the law's punitive measures force them to restrict Grok Imagine's image-editing features.
The lawsuit centers on the claim that the state statute violates the First Amendment.

stories.title: Musk went to “war,” sought jail time for X ad boycotts—but case ends with a whimper
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Elon Musk's legal pursuit against X ad boycotts concluded without a major ruling.
The dispute resulted in advertisers agreeing to 'reset' their relationship with the platform.
The story highlights ongoing tensions between X's operational changes and advertiser sentiment.

stories.title: Who wins and who loses after US bans foreign robots?
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: A proposed US government ban on foreign-made robots is the central topic.
The article argues that this ban could negatively impact, rather than boost, the domestic US robotics industry.
The piece analyzes the potential economic and technological ramifications of the regulatory action.

stories.title: Google's "privacy-preserving" age verification system is coming to the Play Store
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is rolling out a new age verification API for the Play Store.
The system is marketed as 'privacy-preserving'.
Implementation relies on parents setting age ranges via Google Family Link.

stories.title: The Social Cost of an AI Teammate: How an Artificial Teammate Reshapes Human-Human Communication in Small-Team Decision-Making
stories.author: Spencer JaQuay
bullet_points: Investigates the sociocognitive impact of integrating Conversational AI as a teammate in small-team decision-making.
Uses a randomized controlled study involving moral-dilemma tasks to compare AI-augmented teams versus all-human teams.
Analyzes communication dynamics through Group Communication Analysis (GCA), surveys, and discourse analysis.

stories.title: Improving Item Discoverability in e-Commerce Search via Related Intent Generation
stories.author: Tejaswi Tenneti
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of traditional e-commerce search systems which prioritize strict query matching over item discoverability.
Proposes a scalable system for 'discovery-augmented search' using intent-conditioned recall expansion.
Focuses on improving user satisfaction by surfacing substitute, complementary, and related items, particularly relevant in grocery e-commerce.

stories.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
stories.author: Hua Wu
bullet_points: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agents.
Focuses on long-horizon office-suite tasks, moving beyond simple task completion.
Adds 'economic grounding' to the evaluation, assessing agent performance relative to cost.

stories.title: Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark
stories.author: Shyamal Lakhanpal
bullet_points: Addresses a critical flaw in standard Conformal Prediction (CP) when applied to high-stakes, imbalanced datasets.
Demonstrates that standard CP severely under-covers rare, costly minority classes (e.g., in fraud or healthcare).
Proposes a solution involving Cost-Sensitive CP and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for robust uncertainty quantification.

stories.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use
stories.author: Lutz Oettershagen
bullet_points: Widespread use of LLMs for text drafting and revision risks creating 'linguistic monoculture'.
This monoculture suggests a potential reduction in population-level variation in linguistic style.
The research introduces a mathematical framework to model authors and LLMs as distributions over linguistic features.

stories.title: Do You Really Need to Pretrain Q-Functions for Online RL Fine-Tuning?
stories.author: Chelsea Fin
bullet_points: Challenges the conventional wisdom in Reinforcement Learning (RL) regarding the necessity of pre-training Q-functions.
Presents evidence that online RL can achieve high performance and reliability even with a randomly initialized Q-function.
Suggests a potential simplification or alternative to the standard pre-training followed by fine-tuning paradigm in value-based RL.

stories.title: Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark
stories.author: Shyamal Lakhanpal
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in standard Conformal Prediction (CP) for high-stakes systems: severe under-coverage of rare, costly minority classes.
Proposes Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention to improve reliability under severe class imbalance.
Benchmarks the proposed methods across critical domains including credit scoring, fraud detection, and healthcare.

stories.title: Mental World Modeling
stories.author: Yiran Zhao
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current world models, which only predict physical states.
It proposes 'Mental World Modeling' to incorporate hidden mental states like beliefs, intentions, and desires of agents.
This shift is crucial because human behavior is driven by internal mental states, not just observable physical scenes.

stories.title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: Current LLM agents struggle significantly with program synthesis from scratch, even with behavioral oracles.
The research addresses this gap by proposing 'SpecFirst,' which treats behavioral specification elicitation as a distinct, crucial step.
Existing synthesis frameworks are criticized for conflating documentation reading, behavioral exploration, and code synthesis into a single, ineffective pass.

stories.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
stories.author: Hua Wu
bullet_points: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLM agents.
The benchmark focuses on long-horizon, real-world office-suite tasks, moving beyond simple conversational tests.
A key innovation is the inclusion of 'task-level economic grounding' to assess the cost-effectiveness of the agents.

stories.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use
stories.author: Lutz Oettershagen
bullet_points: Widespread reliance on LLMs for text generation and revision may lead to 'linguistic monoculture.'
This phenomenon suggests that shared LLM usage could reduce natural variation in how people write and communicate.
The research proposes a mathematical framework to model the interaction between authors and LLMs as distributions over linguistic features.

stories.title: Setoka: A Benchmark for Hierarchical User Understanding in Personalized Agents over Heterogeneous Data
stories.author: Xuan Zhou
bullet_points: Introduces 'Setoka,' a new benchmark designed to test hierarchical user understanding in personalized AI agents.
Addresses a gap in current memory benchmarks, which only test explicit fact retrieval rather than abstract user characteristic inference.
Focuses on the need for agents to handle complex, heterogeneous data for truly effective personalization.

stories.title: Keychron announces first open-source firmware for gaming mice
stories.author: JLO64
bullet_points: Keychron is releasing open-source firmware for its gaming mice.
This move promotes transparency and customization in peripheral hardware.
It represents a shift toward more open ecosystems in the gaming hardware market.

stories.title: Data, Context & RAG Lineage Governance for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.author: jitu028
bullet_points: Focuses on advanced governance for Enterprise AI Agents utilizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Details technical implementations like query-time Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) and cryptographic lineage.
Addresses critical security concerns such as outbound payload sanitization within agentic systems.
